V-SEIHR with seasonality and vaccination.description: Year-long V-SEIHR run on the US population with two interventions composed: seasonality on `transmission_rate` (peak Jan 15, trough Jul 15, matching the Northern Hemisphere defaults from Balcan et al. 2010, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jocs.2010.07.002), and a flat-count vaccination campaign delivered Oct 15 - Dec 31 so the rollout finishes just before the seasonal peak. `output.include_parameters` is enabled so the per-step `transmission_rate` series surfaces in the response for sanity-checking the envelope.

target_parameter.title: Target Parameter
target_parameter.description: Name of the model parameter to transform. Must already be defined in `model.parameters`.

max_date.title: Max Date
max_date.description: Date when the multiplier reaches its peak (1.0), `YYYY-MM-DD`.

min_value.title: Min Value
min_value.description: Lower bound of the seasonal scaling. The multiplier reaches `min_value / max_value` at the trough. With the default `max_value=1`, this is simply the fraction of baseline at the trough (e.g. `0.1` means 10% of baseline).

max_value.title: Max Value
max_value.description: Upper bound of the seasonal scaling. Defaults to `1.0`, which makes the peak exactly equal to the baseline parameter. Only set this if you want to express both bounds in absolute units; the multiplier shape depends only on the ratio `min_value / max_value`.

min_date.title: Min Date
min_date.description: Date of trough, `YYYY-MM-DD`. If set, period = `2 * |min_date - max_date|`. If omitted, period defaults to 365 days.

BalcanTransform.title: BalcanTransform
BalcanTransform.description:
Balcan-style sinusoidal seasonality applied across the simulation timeline (Balcan D et al. J. Comput. Sci. 2010; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jocs.2010.07.002).

The transform is **multiplicative on top of the baseline parameter**. At each
step, the existing value of `target_parameter` is multiplied by a sinusoidal
factor that reaches `1.0` on `max_date` (the seasonal peak) and
`min_value / max_value` on `min_date` (the seasonal trough). The effective
parameter therefore swings between `baseline` (peak) and
`baseline * (min_value / max_value)` (trough).

**Recommended usage**: leave `max_value` at its default of `1.0` and only set
`min_value` to express the seasonal floor as a fraction of the baseline. For
example, with `min_value=0.1`, the parameter drops to 10% of its baseline at
the trough.

Setting `max_value` to anything other than `1` only matters if you want to
express both bounds in absolute units (mirroring the notation in Balcan et al.
2010). Note that the multiplier shape depends only on the **ratio**
`min_value / max_value`: `(max_value=0.4, min_value=0.1)` produces exactly
the same dynamics as `(max_value=1, min_value=0.25)` (both have ratio `0.25`).

source.title: Source
source.description: Loads a published population by name from the epydemix data repo.

name.title: Name
name.description: Population name in epydemix, e.g. `United_States`. It should be one of the population available in `GET /populations` endpoint.

age_group_mapping.title: Age Group Mapping
age_group_mapping.description:
Custom age group aggregation. Keys are new group names, values are lists of source age groups to merge.
- Example: `{"0-19": ["0-4", "5-9", "10-14", "15-19"], "65+": ["65-69", "70-74", "75+"]}`.

BuiltinPopulationConfig.title: BuiltinPopulationConfig
BuiltinPopulationConfig.description: Population loaded from the epydemix data repository (countries, regions, etc.).

cached_populations.title: Cached Populations
cached_populations.description: Names of populations currently in cache.

target.title: Target
target.description: Compartment vaccinated individuals move to. `null` marks the source as a dose sink: it contributes to the rate denominator but no transition is emitted.

CompartmentFlow.title: CompartmentFlow
CompartmentFlow.description:
One compartment competing for doses, with an optional vaccinated target.

A flow declares a `source` compartment that contributes to the rate
denominator (the eligible pool that competes for the campaign's doses).
If `target` is set, vaccinated individuals move `source -> target` and
transitions are emitted. If `target` is `null`, the source acts as a
**dose sink**: it absorbs its share of doses (modeling the impossibility
of pre-screening recipients) but no transition is emitted.

Combining flows lets one block model dose competition across multiple
compartments. Examples:

- `[{S, S_vax}]` -- perfect targeting, denominator = S only.
- `[{S, S_vax}, {R, null}]` -- dose waste: denominator = S + R, only
  S -> S_vax fires (matches the upstream epydemix tutorial).
- `[{S, S_vax}, {S_2, S_2_vax}]` -- one budget shared across two
  susceptible strata; each fires its own transition.

layers.title: Layers
layers.description: Contact matrices by layer name. Each matrix is square with one row/column per age group.

overall.title: Overall
overall.description: Combined contact matrix across all layers.

age_groups.title: Age Groups
age_groups.description: Age group labels for matrix indices (same order as rows and columns).

spectral_radius.title: Spectral Radius
spectral_radius.description: Spectral radius (largest eigenvalue) for each layer and overall.

ContactMatrixResponse.title: ContactMatrixResponse
ContactMatrixResponse.description: Response containing contact matrices for a population.

fraction.title: Fraction
fraction.description: Cap as a fraction of the population in `target_age_groups` at campaign `start_date`.

compartments.title: Compartments
compartments.description: Compartments whose current occupancy is summed against the threshold (e.g. `["S_vax","E_vax","I_vax","R_vax"]`).

CoverageCap.title: CoverageCap
CoverageCap.description:
Optional per-campaign cap on cumulative vaccination coverage.

Stops a campaign's contribution to the rate once the current occupancy
of `compartments` (restricted to the parent campaign's
`target_age_groups`) reaches `fraction` of the total population in
those age groups at campaign start.

The check reads current compartment occupancy, not cumulative flow
history, so `compartments` must list every downstream vaccinated state
(including absorbing states like `D_vax`) for the cap to match the
intuitive notion of coverage. The cap is evaluated at the start of
each step, before the binomial draw, so a single step of overshoot is
possible.

source.title: Source
source.description: Defines age groups and contact matrices inline.

age_groups.title: Age Groups
age_groups.description:
Age group label to population count. Insertion order defines the row/column order used by every entry in `contact_matrices`.
- Homogeneous (single group): `{"A": 100000}`.
- Two groups: `{"A": 100, "B": 100}`.

contact_matrices.title: Contact Matrices
contact_matrices.description:
Contact matrices keyed by layer name. The keys define the layer set; each matrix must be square with one row/column per `age_groups` entry, in the same order. Layer name `"overall"` is reserved by epydemix and rejected.
- Homogeneous (1x1): `{"all": [[1.0]]}`.
- Two groups (2x2): `{"all": [[0.2, 0.3], [0.3, 0.2]]}`.

rate.title: Rate
rate.description: Per-day hazard rate applied to each source compartment inside the campaign window.

FixedRateRollout.title: FixedRateRollout
FixedRateRollout.description:
Constant per-day hazard rate across the campaign window.

Inside the active window this is mathematically identical to a
spontaneous transition at `rate`: each individual in a source
compartment (restricted to `target_age_groups`) has a per-day hazard of
`rate` of moving to the corresponding target. Outside the window the
rate is zero. Unlike `flat_count`, the per-day flow scales with the
current source pool rather than being held constant.

daily_doses.title: Daily Doses
daily_doses.description: Doses delivered per day. Naturally capped per group by the available source-compartment population at each step.

FlatCountRollout.title: FlatCountRollout
FlatCountRollout.description:
Constant daily dose count across the campaign window.

Doses are split across `target_age_groups` (on the parent campaign)
proportional to the current source-compartment population in each group
at every simulation step. The multinomial draw inside the simulator
naturally caps each group's transitions at the available source pool.

epydemix_version.title: Epydemix Version
epydemix_version.description: Version of the epydemix library, or None if not available.

initial_percentages.title: Initial Percentages
initial_percentages.description:
Percentage (0-100, not a fraction) of the population in each compartment. Remainder goes to the first compartment.
- Example: `{"I": 0.01, "R": 10.0}` puts 0.01% in `I` and 10% in `R`.

compartments.title: Compartments
compartments.description:
Absolute counts per compartment per age group. Required when method is `absolute`. Each list must have one entry per age group, in the same order as `population.age_groups`.
- Example (two age groups): `{"Susceptible": [9900, 9990], "Infected": [100, 10]}`.

reduction_factor.title: Reduction Factor
reduction_factor.description: Multiplier for contacts. `0.2` = reduce to 20% of normal.

InterventionConfig.title: InterventionConfig
InterventionConfig.description: A contact reduction intervention applied to a specific layer during a time period.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description:
Predefined model preset. Auto-configures compartments and transitions.
- `SIR`: Susceptible-Infected-Recovered
- `SEIR`: Susceptible-Exposed-Infected-Recovered
- `SIS`: Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible
- `V-SEIR`: Vaccinated SEIR with parallel unvaccinated/vaccinated compartments. Use together with the `vaccination` block.
- `V-SEIHR`: Vaccinated SEIHR with parallel unvaccinated/vaccinated compartments. Use together with the `vaccination` block.
When using a preset, you can still override default parameter values via `parameters`.

compartments.title: Compartments
compartments.description:
List of compartment names for a custom model. Required if no preset.
- Example: `["S", "E", "I", "R", "H"]`.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description:
Model parameters as key-value pairs. Each value is one of:
- scalar `float`: uniform constant rate.
- `list[float]`: age-varying (length must match resolved population age groups).
- `str`: arithmetic expression over other parameter names, e.g. `"(1 - p_h) * gamma"`. Evaluated after scalars, age-varying values, and `parameter_transforms`, in dependency order. Only arithmetic operators are supported (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `//`, `**`, `%`, unary `+`/`-`); no function calls, attribute access, subscripts, or comparisons. Source-parameter shapes propagate via numpy broadcasting, so a calculated parameter inherits time- or age-variation from its sources automatically. Calculated parameters cannot be the target of `parameter_transforms` (apply transforms to the source instead). Expressions can also reference reserved SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE names derived from the model state, currently:
- `CONTACT_MATRIX_EIGENVALUE_ALL`: dominant eigenvalue of the sum of all contact-matrix layers. Useful for R0 calibration, e.g. `{"transmission_rate": "R0 * gamma / CONTACT_MATRIX_EIGENVALUE_ALL"}`. User parameter names cannot collide with these reserved names.
For presets, scalar/list values override the preset defaults. For custom models, all parameter names used in transitions must be defined here. Examples:
- Scalar parameter: `{"transmission_rate": 0.3, "recovery_rate": 0.1}`.
- Age-varying parameter: `{"transmission_rate": [0.35, 0.30, 0.25]}`.
- Calculated parameter: `{"p_h": 0.05, "gamma": 0.1, "recovery_rate": "(1 - p_h) * gamma"}`.

transitions.title: Transitions
transitions.description:
List of transitions between compartments. Required if no preset.
Each transition defines how individuals move from one compartment to another.

ModelConfig.title: ModelConfig
ModelConfig.description: Epidemic model configuration. Use `preset` for a built-in model, or provide `compartments`, `parameters`, and `transitions` for a custom model.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: Preset name if a preset was used.

ModelMetadata.title: ModelMetadata
ModelMetadata.description: Model section of simulation metadata. Mirrors the `model` section of the request.

quantiles.title: Quantiles
quantiles.description: Quantiles to compute for trajectories and summary. Default: `[0.025, 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95, 0.975]`.

include_trajectories.title: Include Trajectories
include_trajectories.description: Include raw per-run trajectory data in the response. Can be large.

include_parameters.title: Include Parameters
include_parameters.description: Include the effective per-step parameter arrays under `results.parameters`. Useful for plotting parameters such as `transmission_rate` after balcan/scale/override transforms have been applied. Off by default.

compartments.title: Compartments
compartments.description: Compartments to include in the trajectory section. Default: all. Does not affect `summary`.

transitions.title: Transitions
transitions.description: Transitions to include in the trajectory section. Default: all. Does not affect `summary`.

age_groups.title: Age Groups
age_groups.description: Age groups to include in both trajectories and summary, e.g. `["0-4", "5-19", "total"]`. Default: all age groups plus `total`.

summary.description: Summary statistics configuration. Omit to return the default summary.

OutputConfig.title: OutputConfig
OutputConfig.description: Output configuration. Everything is optional; defaults return all compartments, all transitions, all age groups (including `total`), all standard quantiles, and a populated `summary`.

target_parameter.title: Target Parameter
target_parameter.description: Name of the model parameter to transform. Must already be defined in `model.parameters`.

value.title: Value
value.description: Absolute replacement value during the window. Scalar for uniform, or a list of one value per age group (length must match the resolved population).

OverrideTransform.title: OverrideTransform
OverrideTransform.description:
Absolute value override during a date window.

Replaces the parameter wholesale during `[start_date, end_date]`. Applied
last in the transform pass, so an override always wins for its window
regardless of where it appears in the list. The override is baked into
`model.parameters`, so calculated parameters that reference the target
pick up the overridden value automatically (the same as `balcan` /
`scale`).

dates.title: Dates
dates.description: Dates corresponding to values, matching the simulator's internal grid.

data.title: Data
data.description: Nested structure: `parameter_name -> age_group -> [values per date]`. Scalar parameters and time-varying scalars are broadcast across all age groups; age-varying parameters report each group separately. Override windows are baked into the returned arrays so they reflect what actually drove the simulation.

ParameterResults.title: ParameterResults
ParameterResults.description:
Effective parameter values used during the simulation, broadcast to per-step
arrays. Useful for plotting `transmission_rate` vs. time after seasonality, scaling,
or override transforms have been applied. Only present if `include_parameters` was true.

peak_date.title: Peak Date
peak_date.description: Date of the peak from the median trajectory.

PeakStatistic.title: PeakStatistic
PeakStatistic.description: Peak statistic for a compartment in one age group.

age_groups.title: Age Groups
age_groups.description: Default 5-group aggregation (epydemix `mistry_2021`/`prem_2021` coarse groups). Keys are in age-ascending order.

age_distribution.title: Age Distribution
age_distribution.description: Raw per-single-year population counts from the upstream `age_distribution.csv`. Keys are age labels (e.g. `"0"`..`"83"`, `"84+"`) in ascending order.

default_contact_source.title: Default Contact Source
default_contact_source.description: Default contact source for this population.

available_layers.title: Available Layers
available_layers.description: Available contact layers (e.g. home, work, school, community).

PopulationListResponse.title: PopulationListResponse
PopulationListResponse.description: Response for listing all available populations.

source.title: Source
source.description: Which population branch the request resolved to. `builtin` = loaded from the epydemix data repo; `custom` = supplied inline.

contacts_source.title: Contacts Source
contacts_source.description: Resolved contact matrix source actually used. `null` for custom populations.

age_group_mapping.title: Age Group Mapping
age_group_mapping.description: Custom age group aggregation, echoed back if the request supplied one. `null` for custom populations.

age_groups.title: Age Groups
age_groups.description: Age group label to population count, e.g. `{"0-4": 18608139}`. Keys are in model (age-ascending) order.

contact_matrices.title: Contact Matrices
contact_matrices.description: Per-layer contact matrices actually used by the simulation, keyed by layer name. Row/column order matches `age_groups` insertion order.

PopulationMetadata.title: PopulationMetadata
PopulationMetadata.description: Population section of simulation metadata. Mirrors the `population` section of the request and adds resolved/derived values.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Default parameter values. A list value means the default is age-stratified (one entry per age group on the resolved population).

PresetInfo.title: PresetInfo
PresetInfo.description: Information about a predefined epidemic model.

PresetsListResponse.title: PresetsListResponse
PresetsListResponse.description: Response listing all available model presets.

target_parameter.title: Target Parameter
target_parameter.description: Name of the model parameter to transform. Must already be defined in `model.parameters`.

ScaleTransform.title: ScaleTransform
ScaleTransform.description:
Multiplicative scaling applied during a date window.

Outside `[start_date, end_date]` the multiplier is 1.0; inside it is
`factor`. Composes multiplicatively with other transforms on the same
parameter in the order listed.

model.description: Model configuration used for the run.

population.description: Resolved population configuration and derived counts.

simulation.description: Simulation execution parameters used for the run.

interventions.title: Interventions
interventions.description: Contact-reduction interventions applied to the run, echoed from the request.

parameter_transforms.title: Parameter Transforms
parameter_transforms.description: Parameter transforms applied to the run, echoed from the request.

vaccination.description: Vaccination configuration applied to the run, echoed from the request.

SimulationMetadata.title: SimulationMetadata
SimulationMetadata.description: Metadata about the simulation run, grouped to mirror the request shape.

population.title: Population
population.description: Population configuration. It can load preset population from epydemix, or a custom population defined inline.

initial_conditions.description: Initial conditions. Defaults to a small infected fraction.

parameter_transforms.title: Parameter Transforms
parameter_transforms.description:
Parameter transforms applied to model parameters. Three methods are supported:
- `balcan`: sinusoidal seasonality across the simulation timeline (multiplicative).
- `scale`: multiplicative factor over a date window.
- `override`: absolute replacement over a date window (scalar or per-age-group).
Multiple transforms on the same parameter compose: `balcan` and `scale` stack multiplicatively in the order listed; `override` always wins for its date window, regardless of position in the list.

vaccination.description: Vaccination rollout. Defines the source → target flow and any number of dose-count campaigns. The vaccinated compartment structure and vaccine efficacy (`VE_S`, plus `VE_H` for V-SEIHR) are defined in the model (either via a vaccination preset (V-SEIR, V-SEIHR), or by supplying a custom model with vaccinated twin compartments and calculated parameters).

output.description: Output configuration. Defaults to all compartments/transitions with standard quantiles.

simulation_id.title: Simulation Id
simulation_id.description: Unique identifier for this simulation run.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `completed`. Failed runs return an HTTP error instead: 422 for invalid input, 504 for a population load timeout, 500 for an internal error.

trajectories.description: Raw trajectory data. Only present if `include_trajectories` was true.

parameters.description: Effective per-step parameter arrays. Only present if `include_parameters` was true.

SimulationRunMetadata.title: SimulationRunMetadata
SimulationRunMetadata.description: Simulation section of metadata. Mirrors the `simulation` section of the request.

StatisticQuantiles.title: StatisticQuantiles
StatisticQuantiles.description: Quantile values for a summary statistic, keyed by quantile string (e.g. `0.5`).

peak_compartments.title: Peak Compartments
peak_compartments.description: By default, peak statistics are returned for every compartment. Pass a list to narrow the response, e.g. `["Infected"]`, or pass `[]` to explicitly skip returning this summary. Per-quantile peak values and the median-trajectory peak date are returned for each included age group.

total_transitions.title: Total Transitions
total_transitions.description: By default, cumulative totals are returned for every transition. Pass a list to narrow the response, e.g. `["Susceptible_to_Infected"]`, or pass `[]` to explicitly skip returning this summary. Per-quantile total event counts are returned for each included age group.

SummaryConfig.title: SummaryConfig
SummaryConfig.description:
Configuration for summary statistics.

Summary is returned by default for every compartment and transition, broken
down by age group and by the quantiles requested in `output.quantiles`.
Use the fields below to narrow that down.

TrajectoriesResults.title: TrajectoriesResults
TrajectoriesResults.description: Raw trajectories from all simulation runs.

TrajectoryData.title: TrajectoryData
TrajectoryData.description: Raw trajectory data for a single simulation run.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
Type of transition.
- `spontaneous`: rate is a fixed parameter (e.g. recovery, incubation).
- `mediated`: rate depends on the proportion of a mediating compartment (e.g. transmission driven by contact with infectious individuals).

params.title: Params
params.description:
Parameter name(s) governing this transition.
- Spontaneous: a single parameter name (the rate), e.g. `["recovery_rate"]`.
- Mediated: a two-element list `[rate_param, mediating_compartment]`, e.g. `["transmission_rate", "I"]`.
A single string is also accepted and will be wrapped into a list.

TransitionConfig.title: TransitionConfig
TransitionConfig.description: A single transition between compartments. Transitions define how individuals move between compartments, either spontaneously at a fixed rate or mediated by contact with another compartment.

name.title: Name
name.description: Optional label echoed back in metadata.

end_date.title: End Date
end_date.description: Campaign end (`YYYY-MM-DD`), inclusive. Must be `>= start_date`.

target_age_groups.title: Target Age Groups
target_age_groups.description: Age group labels to target, e.g. `["20-49", "65+"]`. `null` = all groups.

rollout.title: Rollout
rollout.description: Dose-schedule strategy. The `type` discriminator selects the shape; remaining fields are strategy-specific. Supported: `flat_count`, `fixed_rate`.

coverage.description: Optional coverage cap. When set, the campaign stops contributing to the rate once cumulative coverage in `target_age_groups` reaches `fraction` of the initial population in those age groups. Default `null` = uncapped.

VaccinationCampaignConfig.title: VaccinationCampaignConfig
VaccinationCampaignConfig.description: One vaccination campaign: a time window, an age target, and a rollout strategy.

flows.title: Flows
flows.description: Compartments competing for doses, each with an optional `target`. Sources without a `target` act as dose sinks (contribute to the rate denominator but emit no transition). At least one flow must have a non-null `target`. Defaults to `[{source: 'Susceptible', target: 'Susceptible_vax'}]` for the vaccination presets (V-SEIR, V-SEIHR); required for custom models.

campaigns.title: Campaigns
campaigns.description: Campaign windows. Each carries its own rollout strategy; multiple campaigns may overlap and mix strategies. Their per-step dose schedules add.

VaccinationConfig-Input.title: VaccinationConfig
VaccinationConfig-Input.description:
Vaccination rollout block.

`flows` declares which compartments compete for doses and which of them
actually transition. For the vaccination presets (V-SEIR, V-SEIHR) it
defaults to `[{source: 'Susceptible', target: 'Susceptible_vax'}]`.
Custom models must supply it explicitly.

flows.title: Flows
flows.description: Compartments competing for doses, each with an optional `target`. Sources without a `target` act as dose sinks (contribute to the rate denominator but emit no transition). At least one flow must have a non-null `target`. Defaults to `[{source: 'Susceptible', target: 'Susceptible_vax'}]` for the vaccination presets (V-SEIR, V-SEIHR); required for custom models.

campaigns.title: Campaigns
campaigns.description: Campaign windows. Each carries its own rollout strategy; multiple campaigns may overlap and mix strategies. Their per-step dose schedules add.

VaccinationConfig-Output.title: VaccinationConfig
VaccinationConfig-Output.description:
Vaccination rollout block.

`flows` declares which compartments compete for doses and which of them
actually transition. For the vaccination presets (V-SEIR, V-SEIHR) it
defaults to `[{source: 'Susceptible', target: 'Susceptible_vax'}]`.
Custom models must supply it explicitly.
